evidence: dtos.ts defines toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto, which every use case calls; no file maps entities to DTOs inline.
CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStateUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase and TransitionOrderUseCase reach orders only through the injected OrderRepository (findById, findByState, save).
ListStockLevelsUseCase reads products only through ProductRepository.findAll.
Stock reservation goes through StockReservationService.reserve and release, in place-order-use-case.ts and cancel-order-use-case.ts.
Order state rules are called on the domain object (order.cancel(), order.moveTo(target)), not copied into the use cases.
assertExecuteRule in place-order-use-case.ts is the only place customerId is checked.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module's files share one concern: application use cases and DTO mapping for order and stock management. Every use case follows the same pattern: load through a domain port, call a domain behaviour, save through the port, then map with the shared toOrderDto or toStockLevelDto in dtos.ts. Data is reached only through the injected OrderRepository, ProductRepository and StockReservationService ports. No database, ORM or query client is used directly. Order state changes stay in the domain (order.cancel(), order.moveTo(target)). The only application-level validation, assertExecuteRule in place-order-use-case.ts, appears once. Three use cases repeat a short not-found guard, but it is a basic existence check, not a business rule written twice. No candidate flags were raised.
